Title: Designing and evaluating large language model-enabled clinical decision support for heart failure: a modular and risk-tiered framework
Summary: Proposes and evaluates a modular, risk-tiered framework for embedding LLMs into clinical decision support for heart failure management. The design stratifies recommendations by risk level to balance automation with clinician oversight in high-stakes cardiac care.

Title: Performance of large language models and clinical decision support in perioperative management of oral anticoagulants
Summary: Assesses baseline LLM performance on perioperative anticoagulation management decisions and finds it modest and insufficient to replace clinical judgment alone. Integrating structured clinical decision support tools alongside the LLM produced marked, clinically meaningful improvements in accuracy.
Outcome: clinical decision accuracy for anticoagulation management

Title: Guideline-Integrated Large Language Models Improve Decision Support for Acute Ear, Nose and Throat Emergencies
Summary: Examines whether LLMs can reliably apply specialty guidelines in time-sensitive ENT emergency settings. Retrieval-augmented generation grounded in clinical guidelines improved reliability, safety, and guideline alignment of the LLM's decision-support outputs.

Title: Augmenting clinical decision-making with large language models: evaluation across general and specialty tasks
Summary: Evaluates LLM-augmented clinical decision-making across a range of general and specialty-specific clinical tasks. Compares performance to assess where LLM assistance adds the most value versus where limitations remain.

Title: Advancing Knowledge in Evaluating the Clinical Impact of Large Language Models for Clinical Text Summarization: A Narrative Review
Summary: A narrative review synthesizing evidence on how LLMs are used and evaluated for summarizing clinical text from electronic health records. Discusses methods for assessing clinical impact and highlights persistent concerns about hallucination and omission in generated summaries.

Title: Large Language Models for Clinical Narrative Processing: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
Summary: Reviews methods, applications, and open challenges for using LLMs to process clinical narratives, including information extraction, summarization, triage prediction, and section classification. Notes that LLMs often surpass traditional machine-learning approaches on these tasks but still face challenges around reliability.
Outcome: clinical narrative processing (extraction, summarization, triage, classification)

Title: How Good Are Patient-Facing LLMs at Survivorship Questions? A Comparative User Evaluation Across Four Chatbots
Summary: Compares four patient-facing LLM chatbots on their ability to answer cancer survivorship questions, evaluated by cancer survivors themselves. Identifies trust, accuracy, provenance, personalization, empathy, and risk-based escalation as key themes governing patients' willingness to act on chatbot responses.

Title: Feasibility and user evaluation of HopeBot: An LLM-powered conversational chatbot for depression screening
Summary: Introduces HopeBot, an LLM-powered conversational agent that administers the PHQ-9 depression screening instrument via text or voice with real-time clarification. Reports feasibility and user evaluation results for this patient-facing screening tool.

Title: Impact of Large Language Model-Based AI Tools on Physician-Patient Communication: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining how LLM-based AI tools affect physician-patient communication. Finds that LLM-generated responses tend to be more empathetic, detailed, and understandable, with potential positive effects on patient experience and engagement.

Title: Evaluating Small Open LLMs for Medical Question Answering: A Practical Framework
Summary: Proposes a practical framework for evaluating small, open-weight LLMs on medical question answering, arguing that high average accuracy alone is insufficient. Emphasizes the need for models to consistently return reliable answers across varied clinical questions.

Title: Large Language Models and Adverse Event Detection Within Immunotherapy Clinical Trials
Summary: Evaluates the use of large language models to automatically detect and flag adverse events reported within immunotherapy clinical trial records. Assesses accuracy of LLM-based extraction compared to manual clinical trial safety review.
Outcome: adverse event detection in clinical trials

Title: Large Language Models in Post-Acute and Long-Term Care: Bridging Promise and Practice
Summary: Discusses opportunities and practical barriers to deploying LLMs in post-acute and long-term care settings. Reviews current applications and outlines steps needed to translate promise into routine clinical practice.
Outcome: applications and adoption in post-acute/long-term care

Title: Structured Clinical Input-Guided Large Language Model Workflow for Acute Ischemic Stroke Discharge Education: A Multicenter Feasibility Study
Summary: Tests a multicenter workflow in which structured clinical inputs guide an LLM to generate patient discharge education materials for acute ischemic stroke. Reports on feasibility and quality of the LLM-generated discharge education content.
Outcome: quality of generated discharge education materials

Title: Benchmarking agreement between large language models and published clinical trial conclusions across four artificial intelligence platforms
Summary: Compares ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok3, and Claude on their ability to interpret numerical and statistical results from 20 landmark NEJM randomized controlled trials and reach conclusions matching the published findings. ChatGPT showed the highest concordance (100%), followed by Gemini, Grok3, and Claude, though possible training-data leakage limits interpretation.
Outcome: agreement/concordance with published clinical trial conclusions

Title: LLM-in-the-Loop execution of clinical quality language
Summary: Proposes and evaluates a workflow that keeps a large language model in the loop during execution of clinical quality language for automated quality-measure computation. Examines how LLM assistance affects accuracy and efficiency of clinical quality measure execution.

Title: Large Language Model Performance and Clinical Reasoning Tasks
Summary: Assesses how well large language models perform on structured clinical reasoning tasks compared to expected clinician reasoning pathways. Examines strengths and failure modes of LLM-based clinical reasoning.

Title: Leveraging large language models to enhance cytopathology: Opportunities, challenges, and future directions; a practical review from the ASC Clinical Practice Committee
Summary: A practical review from the American Society of Cytopathology examining how LLMs and vision-language models can support structured reporting, diagnostic assistance, quality control, education, and workflow integration in cytopathology. Discusses current opportunities, challenges, and future directions for adoption.
Outcome: structured reporting and diagnostic assistance in cytopathology

Title: General-purpose large language models outperform specialized clinical AI tools on medical benchmarks
Summary: Compares specialized clinical AI tools (OpenEvidence, UpToDate Expert AI) against frontier general-purpose LLMs (GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6) on MedQA questions, HealthBench items, and real de-identified physician queries. Frontier general-purpose LLMs outperformed the specialized clinical AI tools across all three evaluation stages.
Outcome: medical benchmark / clinical query performance comparison

Title: Clinician Use of a General-Purpose Large Language Model in Hospital Medicine: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study
Summary: A mixed-methods pilot study examining how hospital medicine clinicians actually use a general-purpose LLM in daily practice. Combines usage data with qualitative feedback to characterize adoption patterns, perceived value, and concerns.
Outcome: clinician usage patterns and perceived utility

Title: LLM-as-a-Judge in Healthcare: A Scoping Analysis of Applications, Methods, and Human Alignment
Summary: A scoping analysis of how LLMs are used as automated judges to evaluate other AI outputs or clinical text in healthcare applications. Reviews methods for LLM-as-a-judge and examines how well these automated judgments align with human expert assessment.
Outcome: alignment of LLM-based evaluation with human judgment

Title: Can Large Language Models Identify When an Upper Extremity Problem Needs Nonurgent Attention? An Assessment of Multiple LLM Chatbots
Summary: Presented five LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Copilot, Gemini, and PerplexityChat) with urgent and nonurgent upper-extremity symptom scenarios and assessed whether they correctly identified which needed nonurgent attention. Chatbots identified nonurgent conditions with 97% positive predictive value and 89% negative predictive value, improving to 96% and 97% respectively after follow-up questioning.

Title: Large language models provide unsafe answers to patient-posed medical questions
Summary: A physician-led red-teaming study evaluated 888 responses from four chatbots (Claude, Gemini, GPT-4o, Llama3-70B) to 222 patient-posed medical questions spanning internal medicine, women's health, and pediatrics. Problematic response rates ranged from 21.6% (Claude) to 43.2% (Llama), with unsafe responses ranging from 5% (Claude) to 13% (GPT-4o, Llama).
Outcome: answer safety for patient medical questions

Title: AI-driven Medical Care: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Generating Personalized Stroke Education Materials
Summary: Evaluates the ability of large language models to generate personalized patient education materials for stroke care. Assesses quality and appropriateness of the LLM-generated educational content for stroke patients.
Outcome: quality of generated patient education materials

Title: Assessing large language model responses to pediatric depression FAQs: a cross-sectional study on readability, accuracy, and sentiment
Summary: A cross-sectional study assessing LLM-generated responses to frequently asked questions about pediatric depression across readability, factual accuracy, and sentiment. Aims to characterize the quality of LLM output as a patient/parent information source.

Title: Arkangel AI, OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Medisearch: Are They Objectively up to Medical Standards? A Real-Life Assessment of LLM Chatbots in Health Care
Summary: Four independent-expert clinical vignettes (orthopedics, pediatrics, gynecology, psychiatry) were answered by four conversational AI agents (Arkangel AI, OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Medisearch) and rated by clinicians on an 8-criterion Likert scale. Overall satisfaction ranged from 71.1% to 93% across agents, with significant variability in bias and patient-safety criteria.

Title: Psychiatric Risk Associated With Large Language Model Chatbots: An Emerging Concern
Summary: Discusses emerging reports of psychiatric harm, including psychosis, depression, and suicide, associated with heavy use of LLM chatbots, often marked by delusions reinforced by the model. Raises concern about the psychiatric safety of widely used conversational AI tools.
Outcome: psychiatric safety risk associated with chatbot use

Title: A roadmap for medical large language models: a review of foundations, applications, and challenges
Summary: A review presenting a roadmap for translating medical large language models into clinical practice, organized around six interconnected challenges: hallucination/factual reliability, evaluation/benchmarks/clinical validity, safety/ethics/privacy/regulation, robustness/generalization, knowledge updating/maintenance, and human oversight/workflow integration. Argues that clinical usefulness cannot be judged by benchmark performance alone.
Outcome: clinical translation and deployment readiness of medical LLMs

Title: Using Large Language Models to Audit Model Healthcare Biases
Summary: Uses a Stanford Healthcare red-teaming dataset of prompts, outputs, and expert bias labels to test how model size and prompting technique affect LLM-based bias detection (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, Llama3.3, o1-mini). Found that the smaller o1-mini outperformed GPT-4o in precision (up to 53% higher) and F1 score (up to 10% higher), and that Thread-of-Thought prompting improved bias detection across models.

Title: Large Language Models as Unified Multimodal Learners for Clinical Prediction
Summary: Proposes converting all patient data (free-text and structured) into a single natural-language sequence and fine-tuning a pretrained language model end-to-end for clinical prediction, with no task-specific fusion architecture. Evaluated on in-hospital mortality (MIMIC-III), graft failure prediction, and emergency triage classification, this unified textual approach matched or exceeded task-specific multimodal baselines and outperformed a clinically deployed gradient boosting system on graft failure prediction.
Outcome: mortality prediction, graft failure prediction, triage classification

Title: Characterizing Parental Use of a HIPAA-Compliant Large Language Model Chatbot in Rare Pediatric Diseases: Insights from Think-Aloud Sessions
Summary: Uses think-aloud sessions to characterize how parents of children with rare pediatric diseases use a HIPAA-compliant LLM chatbot to seek information and support. Reports on usability, information needs, and parental experience with the tool.

Title: LLM-assisted systematic review of large language models in clinical medicine
Summary: An LLM-assisted systematic review framework identified 4,609 peer-reviewed studies evaluating LLMs in clinical medicine published between January 2022 and September 2025. Found that most studies used simulated or exam-style scenarios rather than real-world patient data (only 1,048 of studies), with ChatGPT/OpenAI models dominating (65.7% of evaluated models) and patient-facing communication/education the largest application area.
Outcome: landscape and evidence gaps in clinical LLM research

Title: Reasoning in Real World Clinical Care: Why Large Language Models Are Not Yet Safe for Autonomous Clinical Decision Support
Summary: Argues that while LLMs can pass medical licensing exams and rival physicians on curated diagnostic cases, they are not yet safe for autonomous triage of self-presenting, undifferentiated patients with no clinician in the loop. Identifies that current evaluations use complete, well-curated simulations that fail to test reasoning under missing information, and that LLM assistant-like behaviors (credulity, agreeableness, miscalibration) can amplify failure modes.
Outcome: safety assessment of autonomous LLM-based clinical triage/decision support

Title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
Summary: Conducts a systematic sensitivity analysis of general-purpose LLMs (GPT-3.5, Llama3) and medical-specific models (ClinicalBERT, BioLlama3, BioBERT) using the MedMCQA benchmark, testing natural and adversarial prompt perturbations. Found that even minor phrasing changes can alter clinical advice and that targeted adversarial prompts can provoke harmful outputs, showing medical LLMs are not intrinsically robust.
Outcome: robustness/consistency of clinical question-answering under prompt variation

Title: Evaluation of large language model responses to patient questions on oral anticoagulant therapy: a comparative expert assessment
Summary: Compares responses from ChatGPT-4.5, Gemini Pro 2.5, and DeepSeek-V3 to 11 frequently asked patient questions about five oral anticoagulants against expert-derived reference answers. Blinded clinical pharmacists rated all responses on accuracy, clarity, and completeness; ChatGPT-4.5 achieved the highest ratings overall, with warfarin-related queries showing the largest differences between models.
Outcome: quality/accuracy of LLM patient education responses on anticoagulation

Title: Multilingual Evaluation of a Large Language Model-Based Primary Care Chatbot
Summary: Evaluates PCP-Bot, an English-developed GPT-4o-based clinical chatbot that collects patient concerns and generates physician-ready summaries, when used by 31 bilingual participants role-playing patients in English and a second language (Mandarin, Spanish, or Hindi). Assesses whether the chatbot's performance degrades in multilingual clinical settings compared to its native English use.
Outcome: multilingual performance and summary quality of a primary-care chatbot

Title: Large Language Model-Based Behavioral Activation Chatbot for Young People With Depression Using Artificial Users and Clinical Experts: Mixed Methods Evaluation
Summary: Implements a GPT-4o-based chatbot using a structured system prompt to deliver a single-session behavioral activation intervention for people aged 14-29 with depression, generating 48 sessions with AI-simulated artificial users derived from varied clinical vignettes. Independent clinical expert assessment evaluated how well the LLM-based chatbot delivered this structured psychological intervention.
Outcome: feasibility/quality of delivering a structured behavioral therapy intervention

Title: Feasibility of a Large Language Model Chatbot to Support Parental Understanding in the PICU
Summary: Tests a GPT-4o-based, EHR-informed chatbot answering questions from 14 parents of children in the pediatric intensive care unit over 10-minute sessions. Parents showed sustained engagement (median 6 questions/session, 96% positive ratings, NPS +57) and the chatbot's 1,225 generated sentences were 99.3% accurate, with all errors classified as minor, supporting progression to a randomized controlled trial.

Title: Research on patient-facing chatbots based on large language models in the care of older people: a living systematic review
Summary: A living systematic review of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library identified 9 studies (from 1,228 records) on patient-facing LLM chatbots in the care of older people, with a median sample size of 12 older participants. Found that most studies used qualitative methods and none reported effectiveness data from a fully operational deployment, indicating the field remains in an early phase.
Outcome: evidence landscape for LLM chatbots in geriatric care

Title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Triage in Emergency Departments: Seven-Month Retrospective Comparative Study of Natural Language Processing, Large Language Model, and Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures
Summary: Seven-month retrospective study comparing an LLM-based triage architecture (URGENTIAPARSE) against NLP-based, JEPA-based models, and nurse triage in emergency departments. URGENTIAPARSE achieved the best performance (F1 0.900, AUC-ROC 0.879) but showed severe overfitting and selection bias, so external validation is needed before clinical use.

Title: A real-world feasibility evaluation of LLM-based clinical prediction: emergency department return visit admission across two academic medical centers
Summary: Developed and tested a two-stage LLM-based approach at two academic medical centers, in which an LLM first generates structured severity summaries from ED documentation and then predicts return-visit admission via zero-shot/in-context learning. Evaluated feasibility across discrimination, data requirements, operational cost, and hallucination risk to establish a reusable evaluation template for clinical LLM deployment.

Title: Large language models for early childhood caries risk triage: A validation study using standardized pediatric dental vignettes
Summary: Compared Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4 on 50 standardized pediatric dental vignettes (25 high-risk, 25 low-risk) for classifying early childhood caries presentations as warranting immediate referral versus preventive counseling. GPT-4 was found to be a safer and more accessible triage tool than Gemini 2.5 Flash for resource-constrained pediatric dental screening settings.

Title: When algorithms triage trauma: Diagnostic accuracy, undertriage risk, and prompt fragility in frontier large language models
Summary: In an in silico benchmarking study using 150 trauma vignettes, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.0 Flash, and Claude 4.5 Opus showed strong overall trauma triage discrimination, but undertriage occurred disproportionately in geriatric and blunt-trauma scenarios, and 11.2% of repeated prompts (up to 24.5% instability) changed triage category under lexical perturbation. Findings support LLM use only as supervised adjuncts rather than autonomous trauma triage agents.

Title: A multi-agent large language model framework to automatically assess performance of a clinical AI Triage tool
Summary: Used an ensemble of eight open-source LLMs plus GPT-4o to retrospectively evaluate a clinical AI triage tool's detection of intracranial hemorrhage on radiology reports, comparing consensus LLM ratings to human report review. The multi-agent LLM ensemble (best combination: Llama 3.3 70B and GPT-4o) provided a more consistent and reliable ground-truth evaluation than any single LLM, serving as a proof-of-concept for real-time monitoring of deployed clinical AI triage tools.
AI Technique: LLM (multi-agent ensemble: Llama 3.3 70B, GPT-4o, + open-source LLMs)
Outcome: automated evaluation of clinical AI triage tool performance

Title: Large language models for acute coronary syndrome triage at first medical contact in emergency departments
Summary: Developed TriageMaster-70B, an LLM using only patient narratives and vital signs for acute coronary syndrome triage at first medical contact, tested on 16,428 retrospective and 512 prospective ED cases. The model showed high sensitivity and processed cases 39% faster than independent retrospective cardiologist review, suggesting potential for rapid, interpretable ACS triage support.
Outcome: ACS triage sensitivity/speed vs. cardiologist review

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of large language models for emergency department triage: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating LLM performance for emergency department triage found moderate discriminatory performance for identifying the highest-acuity triage category, but limited sensitivity for these critical cases.

Title: When Wrong Answers Matter: Consequence-Weighted Evaluation of Large Language Models for ERCP Triage
Summary: Evaluated GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.0 Pro, and Claude 4 Opus on guideline-based ERCP triage decisions using zero-shot prompts; GPT-5.5 achieved the highest accuracy (96.0%) and near-perfect agreement (kappa 0.92), versus Claude 4 Opus's weaker performance (84.0% accuracy, most under-triage errors). Clinically meaningful differences between models emerged when errors were weighted by procedural delay and safety consequences rather than accuracy alone.

Title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in the Diagnosis, Urgency Triage, and Initial Management of Ophthalmic Emergencies
Summary: Evaluated multiple large language models on diagnosis, urgency triage, and initial management recommendations for ophthalmic emergency scenarios. All models achieved diagnostic accuracies above 80% and gave management advice consistent with recognized ophthalmology guidelines, with no significant performance differences between models.
Outcome: diagnosis/urgency triage accuracy for ophthalmic emergencies

Title: Evaluating large language models for structuring cardiology reports: a real-world clinical study on patient subtyping and trial recruitment
Summary: Used GPT-4.1 to extract structured clinical information from cardiology discharge letters for patient subtyping and clinical trial eligibility assessment in a real-world clinical setting. The model achieved high information-extraction accuracy (0.94±0.08) with low false-negative/false-positive rates for most trial eligibility criteria, supporting practical use of LLMs in clinical trial recruitment workflows.
Outcome: structured information extraction accuracy for trial eligibility/patient subtyping

Title: DxDirector: an agentic large language model driving the full-process clinical diagnosis
Summary: Researchers developed DxDirector-7B, an agentic LLM that autonomously drives the full clinical diagnostic workflow using a stepwise "deep thinking" reasoning process, evaluated on 160 real-world and rare-disease cases across 9 clinical departments against simulated patient/specialist agents. DxDirector-7B achieved higher diagnostic accuracy than larger state-of-the-art medical and general-purpose LLMs despite its smaller size.

Title: DeepSeek vs ChatGPT vs Claude: benchmarking large language models for clinical diagnosis using a novel ICD-10-CM-based evaluation framework
Journal/Source: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
Summary: Benchmarked DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet on 50 real-world clinical cases from the MultiCaRe dataset using a hierarchical ICD-10-CM-based scoring framework. DeepSeek-V3 achieved the highest diagnostic score (2.32±1.53) and tied GPT-4o for the highest binary diagnostic accuracy (82%), with Claude 3.5 Sonnet performing weakest (76%).
AI Technique: LLM (DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet)

Title: Improving sepsis best practice utility and clinical acceptance using an LLM-enhanced prediction system
Summary: Developed COMPOSER-LLM, which augments an existing sepsis prediction model with an LLM that analyzes clinical notes to add contextual support to sepsis risk alerts in two emergency departments. Evaluated on 2,500 patient encounters, the system achieved 72.1% sensitivity, 52.9% PPV, and an F-1 score of 61.0% with 0.0087 false alarms per patient-hour, outperforming the standalone model and improving nurses' perceived acceptance of the alerts.

Title: CLIN-LLM: A safety-constrained hybrid framework for clinical diagnosis and treatment generation
Summary: Proposed CLIN-LLM, a hybrid pipeline combining a fine-tuned BioBERT classifier for uncertainty-aware disease diagnosis from symptoms/vitals with retrieval-augmented treatment generation checked against a drug-drug interaction database. The system achieved 98% diagnostic accuracy/F1 (7.1% better than ClinicalBERT), 78% top-5 retrieval precision, and reduced unsafe antibiotic suggestions by 67% versus GPT-5.

Title: Performances of five large language models in clinical decision-making for internal medicine: A comparative study
Summary: Compared five LLMs (including GPT, O1, Gemini, and Claude) on 405 internal medicine cases across nine subspecialties, with two senior clinicians rating outputs on diagnosis, differential diagnosis, examinations, and treatment. GPT, O1, and Gemini performed best overall while Claude performed worst, and all models showed weaknesses in differential diagnosis and respiratory disease management.
AI Technique: LLM (GPT, O1, Gemini, Claude, and others)

Title: Large-language-models for pediatric diagnosis: Performance evaluation using real-world clinical notes from common and rare cases
Summary: Compared four LLMs (DxGPT/GPT-4, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, o1-preview) against 78 pediatric clinicians on 50 real clinical cases (25 rare, 25 common) from a tertiary pediatric hospital. Newer LLMs outperformed earlier models and human clinicians on complex pediatric diagnostics, particularly for rare diseases, though response consistency remained a concern.

Title: Can Large Language Models Preserve Diagnostic Accuracy Despite Patient Self-Diagnosis and Framing Bias in Hypothetical Upper-Extremity Scenarios?
Summary: Tested GPT-5 on 180 randomized hypothetical vignettes across five common upper-extremity musculoskeletal conditions to assess whether patient self-diagnosis and framing bias affected diagnostic accuracy. The model correctly identified the intended diagnosis in 92% of scenarios regardless of patient self-diagnosis, and appropriately deviated from incorrect patient-proposed diagnoses in 89% of the cases where it disagreed.
Disease: de Quervain tendinopathy, rotator cuff tendinopathy, lateral epicondylitis, trigger digit, trapeziometacarpal arthritis

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Psychiatry Training: Comparative Insights from Nine Large Language Models Across Cultural and Exam Contexts
Summary: Compared nine LLMs (ChatGPT-5, ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet-4/4.5, Gemini-2.5 Flash/Pro, Grok-3/4, DeepSeek-v3) on 100 psychiatry exam questions spanning USMLE-type, TUS-type, and expert-authored formats. Accuracy varied by question format (83.8% USMLE-type vs. 95.6% TUS-type vs. 92.1% expert-authored), with premium models showing higher temporal consistency than free versions.
AI Technique: LLM (ChatGPT-5, ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet-4/4.5, Gemini-2.5, Grok-3/4, DeepSeek-v3)

Title: Generative artificial intelligence in clinical reasoning and differential diagnosis in internal medicine
Summary: Narrative review examining how generative AI/LLMs affect diagnostic reasoning in internal medicine, covering optimal clinician-LLM interaction design, timing of AI consultation, safe integration models, and key risks. Concludes that LLMs improve differential diagnosis when used by trained professionals within structured workflows, but passive use can introduce bias and clinician-AI collaboration does not always outperform autonomous LLM use.

Title: Multi-Axial Analysis of Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Inter-Verifier Disagreement and Its Implications for Automated Evaluation
Summary: Evaluated three generator LLMs on 1,000 MIMIC-IV hospital-stay cases across four reasoning axes, with evidence-conclusion coherence judged independently by three frontier verifier LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.4 mini). Found that models can score well on reference-based metrics yet produce unsupported rationales, and that inter-verifier agreement on coherence was consistently low (Fleiss' kappa 0.087-0.223), undermining LLM-as-judge evaluation approaches.
AI Technique: LLM (HuatuoGPT-o1-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B; verifiers: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.4 mini)

Title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Multimodal Large Language Models in Retinal Fundus Photography
Summary: Compared four multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5, Grok-2) on 800 color fundus photographs across 8 retinal disease categories. ChatGPT achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (75%, 603/800), far exceeding Claude (18%), Grok (18%), and Gemini (14%), with performance still short of clinical safety standards.
Outcome: retinal disease diagnostic accuracy from fundus images

Title: Comparative evaluation of four large language models (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet-4, and DeepSeek-R1) for diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making in real-world otolaryngology scenarios
Summary: Evaluated four LLMs on 100 real otolaryngology patient cases for diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making. ChatGPT-5 achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (99%), followed by Gemini 2.5 Pro (98%), Claude Sonnet-4 (94%), and DeepSeek-R1 (92%).
AI Technique: LLM (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet-4, DeepSeek-R1)

Title: Diagnostic capability of large language models in critically ill patients: a prospective single-centre study comparing ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini with emergency physicians
Summary: Prospective single-centre observational study comparing stage-wise diagnostic outputs of four LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro) against emergency physicians in critically ill emergency department patients.
AI Technique: LLM (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro)
Outcome: diagnostic agreement with emergency physicians in critical illness

Title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Commercial Large Language Models for Anogenital Skin Lesion Images: A Comparative Study of Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT
Summary: Tested Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT on 218 anogenital skin lesion images for STI binary classification and differential diagnosis. Gemini achieved the highest accuracy for STI binary classification (76.2%) and differential diagnosis (top-1 39.0%, top-3 54.6%, top-5 60.6%), outperforming ChatGPT and Claude.

Title: Comparative performance of chatgpt and gemini in diagnostic classification and clinical reasoning for open-angle glaucoma: a standardized scenario-based study
Summary: Standardized scenario-based study comparing ChatGPT (GPT-5.3) and Gemini on diagnostic classification and clinical reasoning for open-angle glaucoma. GPT-5.3 showed higher consistency and more stable reasoning patterns than Gemini across scenarios.

Title: Agentic GPT-5.0 system outperforms standard large language models and human experts in critical care clinical decision-making: a simulation study
Summary: Simulation study evaluating an agentic GPT-5.0 system against standard LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini) and human critical care specialists on acid-base disorder diagnosis. The agentic system achieved 91.0% overall accuracy versus 78.0% (GPT-4o), 74.5% (Gemini), and 83.0% (human specialists).
Outcome: acid-base disorder diagnostic accuracy in critical care

Title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance
Summary: Introduced PhysAssistBench, a bilingual benchmark of 1,296 physician-validated multi-turn scenarios built from real MIMIC-IV cases, testing LLMs on coordinating physician intent resolution, ambiguous patient communication, and FHIR-based EHR tool use in a single interaction. Found that leading LLMs score well turn-by-turn but reliability collapses across full four-turn physician-patient-EHR sessions.

Title: sebis at CRF Filling 2026: A Two-Stage Local LLM Pipeline for Medical CRF Filling
Summary: Proposed a fully local, domain-adapted two-stage pipeline using MedGemma-27B for the CL4Health 2026 shared task on filling medical Case Report Forms from clinical text, separating binary presence classification from value extraction. Achieved a macro-F1 of 0.55 on the English test track, placing 2nd among fully local/open-source systems.
Outcome: clinical case report form field extraction accuracy (macro-F1)

Title: Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions of Large Language Models in Health Care Communication: Scoping Review
Summary: Scoping review of 96 studies (Jan 2018-Nov 2025) identifying four patterns of LLM use in health care communication: transforming medical information, facilitating dynamic interaction, empowering communication capabilities, and optimizing clinical workflows. Found a paradigm shift from static information processing to dynamic intelligent interaction, but highlighted technical reliability, trust, and integration challenges.

Title: Large Language Models for Health Knowledge Modelling in Data Interoperability: A Scoping Review of Methods, Standards, and Applications
Journal/Source: Studies in Health Technology and Informatics
Summary: Scoping review of 20 studies (from 166 records) on LLMs applied to ontology alignment, terminology mapping, schema integration, and knowledge-graph construction for healthcare data interoperability. Most studies used GPT-4 or BERT-derived models with retrieval-augmented or embedding-based methods, reporting gains in mapping precision and scalability across FHIR, OMOP, and UMLS standards.

Title: Development and Evaluation of a Custom GPT-Based Artificial Intelligence Clinical Decision Support System for Emergency Department Interdepartmental Consultation Automation
Summary: Developed a custom GPT-based, knowledge-guided documentation support system that drafts emergency department interdepartmental consultation requests from minimal free-text clinician input, using public medical knowledge datasets to constrain output structure. Evaluated on 22 de-identified ED consultation scenarios, the system produced structured consultation drafts with feasible department-recommendation concordance, supporting workflow integration.

Title: Can Small Open-Source Language Models With Retrieval-Augmented Generation Match GPT-4 Performance in Breast Cancer Clinical Decision Support?
Summary: Built a domain-specialized RAG pipeline over 1,356 ASCO breast cancer guideline documents and evaluated five LLMs (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, Qwen2.5-14B, LLaMA3-8B, OpenBioLLM-8B) with and without RAG on 98 expert-curated question-answer-context triplets. RAG improved performance for most models, but GPT-4-turbo and Qwen2.5-14B with RAG achieved the highest win counts, with GPT-4 remaining the top performer overall.
AI Technique: LLM (GPT-4-turbo, Qwen2.5-14B, LLaMA3-8B, OpenBioLLM-8B with RAG)

Title: Assessing GPT-4o in cataract surgery decision-making: appropriateness, consistency, and clinical implications
Summary: Retrospective study of 74 cataract patients (146 eyes) processed preoperative clinical, biometric, and lifestyle data through GPT-4o to generate intraocular lens (IOL) recommendations, comparing them against expert consensus and high-/low-volume surgeon selections using kappa and ICC. GPT-4o showed moderate appropriateness and agreement for routine monofocal IOL selection but limited appropriateness and consistency in complex, customized surgical scenarios.

Title: Large language models as clinical decision-support tools in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders: A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and neurologists
Journal/Source: Multiple Sclerosis Journal - Experimental, Translational and Clinical
Summary: Compared ChatGPT-4o (with and without retrieval-augmented generation) against 290 practicing neurologists on 21 clinical vignettes covering MS therapy escalation, AQP4-IgG positive NMOSD management, and serum neurofilament light chain integration. ChatGPT-4o with RAG achieved significantly higher guideline adherence than neurologists (80.5% vs. lower rates) and showed reduced therapeutic inertia.
Disease: multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder

Title: Evaluating large language models for interpreting and applying caries guidelines in clinical decision support
Summary: Systematically evaluated GPT-4o, Grok-3, and DeepSeek on their ability to interpret and translate the ADA's nonrestorative caries management guideline using zero-shot prompting, generating guideline summaries and diagnosis/treatment plans for three standardized clinical cases. GPT-4o showed particularly strong performance in complex clinical reasoning, though all models showed variability in personalized recommendations and occasional mechanistic guideline application.

Title: Developing AI-powered virtual patient chatbots for diagnostic reasoning training
Summary: Developed NLP-based virtual patient chatbots simulating physician-patient interactions across three clinical scenarios (fatigue, stomach ache, memory loss), grounded in dual-process and memory models of diagnostic reasoning, for medical student training. Learners rated the chatbots as effective (4.50/5) and usable (4.46/5) for practicing diagnostic reasoning, citing benefits for hypothesis generation and pattern recognition.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Education: A Comparative Evaluation of Chatbot Reliability After Total Hip Arthroplasty
Summary: Compared responses from multiple AI chatbots (including ChatGPT and Gemini) to frequently asked patient questions about post-total hip arthroplasty care across reliability, quality, accuracy, and readability domains. Gemini scored highest on inter-rater reliability (ICC=0.71), while ChatGPT models showed moderate-to-good reliability (ICC 0.67-0.71) and ChatGPT-3.5 achieved the best readability.

Title: A specialized reasoning large language model for accelerating rare disease diagnosis: a randomized AI physician assistance trial
Summary: Developed RaDaR, an open-source 32B-parameter reasoning LLM trained on ~49,000 real and ~105,000 synthetic rare-disease cases, and evaluated it in a randomized AI physician assistance trial plus a retrospective cohort across four external validation centers. RaDaR outperformed larger open-source models including the 671B DeepSeek-R1, and in the retrospective cohort prioritized the correct final diagnosis before clinical suspicion in 61.06% of cases, a potential lead time of 1.87 months.

Title: Surgical Alignment in Knowledge Graph Training for Clinical Diagnosis with Large Language Models
Summary: Systematically studied five knowledge-graph task formulations, three training paradigms, two knowledge graphs, and three base LLMs to ground LLM reasoning in clinical diagnosis. Introduced Gradient Intervention Density and Gradient Distortion metrics, finding that sparse, localized parameter updates ("surgical alignment") preserve pretrained reasoning better than broader fine-tuning while improving diagnostic knowledge transfer.

Title: Uncertainty Reasoning with Large Language Models for Explainable Disease Diagnosis
Summary: Proposed a neuro-symbolic framework that embeds patient narratives and clinical guidelines into a fuzzy-logic symbolic knowledge base, using an LLM to extract structured medical entities and temporal relations, then applying logic-programming-based inference verification for diagnosis. The two-stage approach (inductive symbolic generalization plus inference verification) produced transparent, human-readable diagnostic reasoning chains with calibrated confidence scores under incomplete or vague patient observations.
